speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the nature and timing of the shooting ear pain, and did this issue start immediately after your tympanoplasty or develop later?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you notice any visible redness, swelling, or discharge at the earring piercing site, and does the pain radiate to the jaw or temple when you chew? I also need to know if you have any history of temporal mandibular joint (TMJ) issues or teeth grinding.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Let me examine your ear canal and the tympanic membrane for any signs of perforation, infection, or granulation tissue. I will also palpate your temporomandibular joint to check for tenderness or clicking that might suggest TMJ dysfunction.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: History of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. Underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks prior. Social history: Works as a cashier at a local department store.

speaker: Doctor
text: I observe a healthy, intact tympanic membrane with no signs of infection or granulation tissue. Upon palpation, your TMJ is tender and exhibits clicking, which suggests the pain is likely referred from the jaw rather than the ear surgery itself. DIAGNOSIS READY: Temporomandibular Joint Disorder (TMD)
